title: One step of the write sweep
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $E$ inject the symbols of $\Gamma$ together with blank into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits, and let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding. Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$, and let $a$ be an action over $\Gamma$ with the same number of work tapes as $M$. For $j\in\{0,\ldots,N\}$ with $j\ne 0$, one step of the binary block-code simulator from the write-sweep configuration at counter $j$ equals the write-sweep configuration at counter $j-1$, for the same $c$ and $a$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is an injection from symbols of $\Gamma$ together with blank into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits
$M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$c$ is a configuration on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$
$a$ is an action for the number of work tapes and state type of $M$
replaced:
For a counter $j \neq 0$, one transition of the binary block-code simulator applied to
the write-sweep configuration (source configuration $c$, source action $a$) at counter
$j$ yields the write-sweep configuration at counter $j-1$: on each tape the entry at
offset $j$ of the code of the effective new symbol is written and the head moves one
cell left.
